notes: Alignment was by passage and rule. Main disagreements: (1) document stance of AI-001 (A delegates, B permit), resolved to permit because the policy allows AI use with conditions and never hands the decision to instructors. (2) unit_stance: coder A coded many procedural duties (risk and impact assessment, training, procurement, monitoring) as require; resolved to neutral because they take no position on AI use. (3) Type choices among P80, P98, P77 and P65 for AI-governance duties, resolved by who the sentence is about (a named role is P80, registration and monitoring are P98, pre-deployment review is P65). (4) Label synthetic media: P103 vs UNCOVERED, resolved to UNCOVERED. (5) Actor all vs student/admin on listed items, and phase differences (before-course vs course-start or general), resolved by re-reading each sentence. (6) Granularity: A split lists (misuse concerns, uses, syllabus items, monitoring duties) into more units than B, giving 27 A-only units, all real statements and all kept; B had 5 B-only units, all kept. Two sentences were split into two units because they held two rules (the bias paragraph; "modify as you see fit and align to ... learning objectives"), adding 2 final units. Shares are over matched units and cover only actor, phase, modality and policy_type.
